No GO TO, ALTER or PERFORM THRU in this program

program_narrative: DB2ERR is a called DB2 error-handling subprogram (PROCEDURE DIVISION USING LS-ERROR-REQUEST) that services one of three request functions chosen by the caller in LS-FUNCTION. For 'LOG ' it builds an error-log row (timestamp, calling program, error type 'D', a severity and retry recommendation derived from the SQLCODE, a 'SQLCODE: ... STATE: ...' code string, message, process date and time, additional info) and inserts it into the DB2 table ERRLOG. For 'DIAG' it translates the caller's SQLCODE into a diagnostic message and return code (deadlock and timeout 4, duplicate key 8, connection error 12, other negative codes 12, non-negative codes 4). For 'RETR' it selects the most recent ERRLOG row for the calling program and returns its message and severity. Any other function code, and a failed ERRLOG insert, are routed to 9000-ERROR-ROUTINE, which sets return code 12 and calls the common error processor ERRPROC with ERR-MESSAGE. The program has no loops and no unstructured flow; it returns to the caller with GOBACK.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN
pseudocode: -- Main dispatcher: route the caller's request by function code LS-FUNCTION
ELSE IF function code is 'DIAG' (FUNC-DIAG) THEN
ELSE IF function code is 'RETR' (FUNC-RETR) THEN
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Main dispatcher: route the caller's request by function code LS-FUNCTION
IF function code is 'LOG ' (FUNC-LOG) THEN
  CALL 1000-log-error
ELSE IF function code is 'DIAG' (FUNC-DIAG) THEN
  CALL 2000-diagnose-error
ELSE IF function code is 'RETR' (FUNC-RETR) THEN
  CALL 3000-retrieve-error
ELSE
  SET err_text = 'Invalid function code'
  CALL 9000-error-routine
END IF
RETURN to caller  -- GOBACK

annotations.note: EVALUATE TRUE over the 88-level names of LS-FUNCTION, translated as an IF / ELSE IF chain

paragraphs.name: 1000-LOG-ERROR
pseudocode: -- Build an ERRLOG row from the caller's error details, then insert it
CLEAR ws_errlog_rec  -- INITIALIZE: alphanumeric items to spaces, numeric items to zero
SET ws_current_timestamp = [runtime: system timestamp]  -- ACCEPT ... FROM TIME STAMP (see annotation)
SET el_program_id = ls_program_id  -- calling program name
CALL 1100-set-severity  -- derive el_error_severity and the retry flag from ls_sqlcode
SET ws_formatted_sqlcode = ls_sqlcode  -- numeric-edited display form PIC -Z(8)9
CONCATENATE 'SQLCODE: ' + ws_formatted_sqlcode + ' STATE: ' + ls_sqlstate INTO el_error_code
-- COBOL STRING DELIMITED BY SIZE: whole items joined; EL-ERROR-CODE is PIC X(8), so only the first 8 characters ('SQLCODE:') are stored
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Build an ERRLOG row from the caller's error details, then insert it
CLEAR ws_errlog_rec  -- INITIALIZE: alphanumeric items to spaces, numeric items to zero
SET ws_current_timestamp = [runtime: system timestamp]  -- ACCEPT ... FROM TIME STAMP (see annotation)
SET el_error_timestamp = ws_current_timestamp
SET el_program_id = ls_program_id  -- calling program name
SET el_error_type = 'D'  -- EL-TYPE-DATA (data error)
CALL 1100-set-severity  -- derive el_error_severity and the retry flag from ls_sqlcode
SET ws_formatted_sqlcode = ls_sqlcode  -- numeric-edited display form PIC -Z(8)9
CONCATENATE 'SQLCODE: ' + ws_formatted_sqlcode + ' STATE: ' + ls_sqlstate INTO el_error_code
  -- COBOL STRING DELIMITED BY SIZE: whole items joined; EL-ERROR-CODE is PIC X(8), so only the first 8 characters ('SQLCODE:') are stored
SET el_error_message = ls_error_text
SET el_process_date = [runtime: FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE characters 1-10]
SET el_process_time = [runtime: FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE characters 12-19]
CLEAR el_user_id  -- spaces
SET el_additional_info = ls_additional_info
CALL 1200-insert-error

annotations.note: TIME STAMP is not one of the standard ACCEPT ... FROM sources (DATE, DAY, DAY-OF-WEEK, TIME); the value placed in WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP depends on the compiler/runtime. Recorded verbatim for SME review
STRING into EL-ERROR-CODE PIC X(8): the 9-character literal 'SQLCODE: ' alone overflows the receiver, so the SQLCODE and SQLSTATE values are not stored in EL-ERROR-CODE (no ON OVERFLOW clause)

FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE returns YYYYMMDDHHMMSShh followed by the UTC offset; reference modification (1:10) yields YYYYMMDDHH and (12:8) starts at the second minute digit, so EL-PROCESS-DATE / EL-PROCESS-TIME are not a conventional date and time. Flagged for SME review

paragraphs.name: 1100-SET-SEVERITY
pseudocode: -- Classify the caller's SQLCODE into an error severity and a retry recommendation
SET retry flag = 'Y'  -- LS-SHOULD-RETRY: caller should retry
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Classify the caller's SQLCODE into an error severity and a retry recommendation
SELECT CASE ls_sqlcode
  WHEN ws_deadlock (-911), ws_timeout (-913):
    SET el_error_severity = 2  -- EL-SEV-WARN
    SET retry flag = 'Y'  -- LS-SHOULD-RETRY: caller should retry
  WHEN ws_connection_error (-30081):
    SET el_error_severity = 4  -- EL-SEV-SEVERE
    SET retry flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
  WHEN ws_dup_key (-803):
    SET el_error_severity = 1  -- EL-SEV-INFO
    SET retry flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
  WHEN ws_not_found (+100):
    SET el_error_severity = 1  -- EL-SEV-INFO
    SET retry flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
  ELSE:
    IF ls_sqlcode < 0 THEN
      SET el_error_severity = 3  -- EL-SEV-ERROR
      SET retry flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
    ELSE
      SET el_error_severity = 1  -- EL-SEV-INFO
      SET retry flag = 'N'  -- LS-NO-RETRY
    END IF
END SELECT

annotations.note: The WHEN operands WS-DEADLOCK, WS-TIMEOUT, WS-CONNECTION-ERROR, WS-DUP-KEY and WS-NOT-FOUND are WORKING-STORAGE items with VALUE clauses -911, -913, -30081, -803 and +100; the program never modifies them, so they act as named constants
SET condition-name TO TRUE moves the 88-level value into LS-RETRY-FLAG ('Y' for LS-SHOULD-RETRY, 'N' for LS-NO-RETRY); the flag is returned to the caller through the LINKAGE area

paragraphs.name: 2000-DIAGNOSE-ERROR
pseudocode: -- Translate the caller's SQLCODE into a diagnostic message and return code
SET ls_error_text = 'DB2 connection error - check availability'
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Translate the caller's SQLCODE into a diagnostic message and return code
SELECT CASE ls_sqlcode
  WHEN ws_deadlock (-911):
    SET ls_error_text = 'Deadlock detected - retry transaction'
    SET ls_return_code = 4
  WHEN ws_timeout (-913):
    SET ls_error_text = 'Timeout occurred - retry transaction'
    SET ls_return_code = 4
  WHEN ws_connection_error (-30081):
    SET ls_error_text = 'DB2 connection error - check availability'
    SET ls_return_code = 12
  WHEN ws_dup_key (-803):
    SET ls_error_text = 'Duplicate key violation'
    SET ls_return_code = 8
  ELSE:
    IF ls_sqlcode < 0 THEN
      SET ls_error_text = 'Unhandled DB2 error'
      SET ls_return_code = 12
    ELSE
      SET ls_error_text = 'DB2 warning condition'
      SET ls_return_code = 4
    END IF
END SELECT

annotations.note: SQLCODE +100 (not found) has no WHEN of its own here and is reported as 'DB2 warning condition', return code 4

paragraphs.name: 3000-RETRIEVE-ERROR
pseudocode: -- Return the most recent logged error for the calling program
WHERE: program_id = ls_program_id AND error_timestamp = latest error_timestamp logged for ls_program_id  -- subquery; see source line 172 for full SQL
IF sqlcode = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE: row found
paragraphs.pseudocode_text:
-- Return the most recent logged error for the calling program
SQL SELECT error_message, error_severity, additional_info
  FROM: ERRLOG table
  WHERE: program_id = ls_program_id AND error_timestamp = latest error_timestamp logged for ls_program_id  -- subquery; see source line 172 for full SQL
  INTO: el_error_message, el_error_severity, el_additional_info
IF sqlcode = 0 THEN  -- CHECK SQLCODE: row found
  SET ls_error_text = el_error_message
  SET ls_return_code = el_error_severity
ELSE
  SET ls_error_text = 'No error history found'
  SET ls_return_code = 4
END IF

annotations.note: Singleton SELECT with a correlated MAX(ERROR_TIMESTAMP) subquery; if two rows share the latest timestamp DB2 returns SQLCODE -811, which takes the ELSE path ('No error history found')
